phases.label: Atrial contraction
phases.detail: Both atria squeeze a final top-up of blood through the open inlet valves. Ventricular volume reaches its maximum.

phases.label: Isovolumetric contraction
phases.detail: Ventricular pressure shoots up with all four valves shut, so volume does not change. S1 is the inlet valves snapping closed.

phases.label: Ejection
phases.detail: Outlet valves open and blood leaves fast, then slows. Arteries stretch with the pulse wave; the ventricles twist and shorten.

phases.label: Isovolumetric relaxation
phases.detail: Outlet valves close (S2) while the muscle relaxes with every valve shut. Pressure falls sharply at constant volume.

phases.label: Filling
phases.detail: Inlet valves open and the ventricles refill, first quickly then slowly. Coronary flow is highest here.

numbers.label: Resting heart rate
numbers.note: Athletes are often lower at rest.

numbers.label: Stroke volume
numbers.note: Blood ejected by one ventricle per beat.

numbers.label: Cardiac output
numbers.note: Heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.

numbers.label: Blood pressure
numbers.note: Systolic over diastolic in the brachial artery.

numbers.label: Ejection fraction
numbers.note: Share of end-diastolic volume that is ejected.

numbers.label: Cycle length
numbers.note: At 75 bpm, with systole shorter than diastole.

numbers.label: AV node delay
numbers.note: Lets the atria finish before the ventricles start.

numbers.label: Coronary flow
numbers.note: Most left ventricular flow happens in diastole.

presets.label: Exercise
presets.note: Sympathetic drive: faster, stronger, shorter diastole.

presets.label: Sleep
presets.note: Vagal dominance with a long filling time.
